purpose: Close the final canonical movement gaps exposed by governed program-name resolution while explicitly preserving program-owned choice and non-exercise control labels.

exercises.purpose: Low-spinal-load hip-hinge accessory used to train glute/hamstring hip extension without turning the slot into another heavy barbell hinge.
coachingCues: Face away from the cable with the line of pull between the legs
unlock the knees and push the hips back
keep ribs stacked and spine neutral
stand by driving the hips through
finish tall without leaning back
commonMistakes: Turning the movement into a squat
rounding the low back
pulling with the arms
overextending at lockout
using more load than the hinge position can control

exercises.purpose: Bench-press variation that removes bounce and reinforces control, position and force production from a deliberate dead-stop pause on the chest.
coachingCues: Use the same stable bench setup as the competition-style press
lower under control to the normal touch point
hold the pause without relaxing the upper back
keep wrists stacked over forearms
press back and up without heaving the bar
commonMistakes: Letting the bar sink into the chest during the pause
losing scapular tension
lifting the butt to restart the bar
bouncing before the pause is established
turning every paused rep into a grinder

exercises.purpose: Short general hip-mobility slot used before testing or on recovery days. The programmed job is to improve comfortable usable hip motion without adding fatigue or forcing a single drill when the athlete needs a different pain-free opener.
coachingCues: Choose a comfortable hip-opening motion appropriate to the day
move slowly through pain-free range
keep the pelvis and ribs controlled
use relaxed breathing rather than forcing depth
finish feeling looser rather than fatigued
commonMistakes: Forcing end range
working through hip pinching or sharp pain
turning the mobility slot into loaded training
using ballistic motion before a max-effort test
chasing stretch sensation instead of better movement

exercises.purpose: Low-fatigue breathing downshift after recovery movement to reduce unnecessary tension and finish the session in a calm recovery state.
coachingCues: Use a comfortable supported position
keep the jaw and shoulders relaxed
breathe quietly through a comfortable range
let the exhale lengthen naturally without straining
stop if breathing feels light-headed or uncomfortable
commonMistakes: Forcing very large breaths
holding the breath between cycles
shrugging on every inhale
turning the drill into a hard breath-hold challenge
continuing through dizziness
